result:
The proposed answer of 24 is incorrect. The area is $5\pi + 10\sqrt{3} \approx 33.03$.

**Setup.** Using the proposed coordinates, $O=(-3,-\sqrt3)$. Shifting so $O$ is the origin gives $S'=(3,\sqrt3)$, $A'=(5,\sqrt3)$, $T'=(6,2\sqrt3)$, $U'=(5,3\sqrt3)$, $R'=(3,3\sqrt3)$, $N'=(2,2\sqrt3)$. The vertices are ordered counterclockwise, and the polar data is:

| Vertex | Angle from $O$ | Distance from $O$ |
|---|---|---|
| $S'$ | $30^\circ$ | $2\sqrt3$ |
| $A'$ | $\alpha=\arctan(\sqrt3/5)\approx 19.1^\circ$ | $2\sqrt7$ |
| $T'$ | $30^\circ$ | $4\sqrt3$ |
| $U'$ | $\gamma=\arctan(3\sqrt3/5)\approx 46.1^\circ$ | $2\sqrt{13}$ |
| $R'$ | $60^\circ$ | $6$ |
| $N'$ | $60^\circ$ | $4$ |

**Method.** The swept region in direction $\varphi$ consists of points at angles $\psi\in[\varphi-45^\circ,\varphi]$ of the original hexagon. The sector is convex because its width is below $180^\circ$, so the radial set at each $\varphi$ is an interval $[m(\varphi),M(\varphi)]$. Therefore
$$\text{Area}=\int_\alpha^{105^\circ}\frac{M(\varphi)^2-m(\varphi)^2}{2}\,d\varphi.$$

Here $M$ is the largest distance from $O$ within the window, and $M=2\sqrt{13}$ whenever $U'$ is in the window. Likewise $m$ is the smallest distance, and $m=2\sqrt3$ whenever $S'$ is in the window. Along the far chain, $f(\psi)$ is $2\sqrt3/\cos(\psi+30^\circ)$ on $[\alpha,30^\circ]$, $4\sqrt3/\sin(\psi+60^\circ)$ on $[30^\circ,\gamma]$, and $3\sqrt3/\sin\psi$ on $[\gamma,60^\circ]$. Along the near chain, $n(\psi)$ is $\sqrt3/\sin\psi$ on $[\alpha,30^\circ]$ and $2\sqrt3/\sin(\psi+60^\circ)$ on $[30^\circ,60^\circ]$.

**Pieces** (with $\Delta=\gamma-\pi/6$):
- $\varphi\in[\alpha,30^\circ]$: $\sqrt3$
- $\varphi\in[30^\circ,\gamma]$: $8\sqrt3-6\Delta$
- $\varphi\in[\gamma,\pi/3]$: $20(\pi/3-\gamma)$
- $\varphi\in[\pi/3,75^\circ]$: $5\pi/3$
- $\varphi\in[75^\circ,\gamma+45^\circ]$: $26\Delta-\sqrt3$, using $\tan(\gamma+60^\circ)=-2\sqrt3$
- $\varphi\in[\gamma+45^\circ,105^\circ]$: $2\sqrt3$

Summing gives $10\sqrt3+20\Delta+25\pi/3-20\gamma$. Substituting $20\Delta = 20\gamma-10\pi/3$ yields
$$\text{Area}=10\sqrt3+5\pi\approx 33.03.$$

**Plausibility check.** The hexagon's own area is $6\sqrt3\approx10.39$. The far vertex sweeps a sector of radius $2\sqrt{13}$ through $45^\circ$, which alone contributes about $20.4$. A total near $33$ is consistent with this.

VERDICT: REJECT
